DriftDetail.description: One system setting whose live value diverged from its declared value.

actual.description: The value the device actually reported.

field.description: The drifted setting, named `<configurator>.<key>` as the device reported it (e.g. `sysctl.net.ipv4.ip_forward`). The configurator qualifies the key because a key names a setting only within its own configurator: two of them may declare the same one, and this list merges by this field.

MachineConfigReference.description: Typed reference to a MachineConfig resource.

namespace.description: Namespace the MachineConfig lives in. Omitted, the referring resource's own namespace is used.

description: Drifted system settings a device reported at check-in. A device's report covers its system settings alone — the answers of the system configurators its profile declares (`sysctl`, `kernelModules`, `macosDefaults`, `windowsRegistry`, ...). Packages, managed files, env vars and aliases are checked on the device by `cfgd diff` and reach the fleet only as the aggregate counts of a compliance summary, never as findings — so a device with no DriftAlert is a device whose system settings matched, not a device proven in sync.

deviceId.description: Identifier of the device that reported the drift, as it enrolled.

driftDetails.description: One entry per drifted system setting, each carrying what was declared and what the device found.

machineConfigRef.description: The MachineConfig whose desired state the device diverged from.

severity.description: How serious the divergence is: `Low`, `Medium`, `High`, or `Critical`. Drives alert routing rather than any automatic remediation.

title: DriftAlertSpec
